explanation: LoadedAdmx lists only loaded ADMX definition files; it has no support definitions (those are in LoadedSupportDefinitions.vb, rule 19624727502016697772). Remove "or support definition". Also state that the guard is on the Enter key only: LsvAdmx_DoubleClick (line 16-18) reads SelectedItems(0) with no check.

Same decision as businessrule-31478983642564096236: Enter calls OpenProductDetails, which exits when nothing is selected (line 59). The rule as written (opens the selected details) drops that condition, and "marks the key as handled" is a UI mechanism (and happens even when nothing is selected). Merge into one rule: Enter or double-click on any of the three lists opens the selected product details, and does nothing when none is selected.

Column layout/width sizing is a display mechanism, not a business rule (the minimum 30 is a layout constant). Drop it; the columns shown (file, folder, namespace) are the only business-facing content.
The Visible guard only avoids refilling while the form is being set up (comment line 24); it changes no outcome for the person. Mechanism, drop it.

The fallback text depends on HasValue: for the policy it is whether the policy names a registry value (line 61), but for a true/false element addList is called with True (line 134), so an element with nothing defined always reads "Left implicit", never "Left to elements". State that.

Merges several decisions per element type and omits some: label presentation text, check box text, list box and multi-text box labels (always shown, even empty), text box and combo box defaults (always shown). Split per element type, or state precisely which parts are conditional (label only for number, text, combo, drop-down; default choice for drop-down only when set; spinner or No spinner). Combo suggestions is already a separate rule.

The wording makes the type look conditional on non-empty; only client extension and registry key are conditional, the type is always shown. Also the lookup (line 118, First) throws if a presentation ID has no matching policy element; say the inspector assumes every presentation ID has a policy element.

says: Double-click on a loaded ADMX file (LoadedAdmx.vb 16-18) and on a support definition (LoadedSupportDefinitions.vb 20-22) opens details with no selection check, unlike the Enter key. Record that the guard exists only for Enter, so double-clicking empty space fails; rules 23966806023143279041 and 19624727502016697772 should say so.

The list editor with names (ListEditor.vb 25-38) takes a key from a cell without handling an empty name: a row with a blank name cell is a null key, so confirming would fail rather than being refused or accepted. Record how a blank or missing name is treated (or that it is unchecked), and that a row in the unnamed list takes only its value cell.
